f.title: Confirm sufficient information shows the drug is acceptably safe before initiating a clinical study
f.statement: Before initiating a clinical study, sufficient information should be available to ensure that the drug is acceptably safe for the planned study in humans.

rows.quote: Before initiating a clinical study, sufficient information should be available to ensure that the drug is acceptably safe for the planned study in humans.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 86 because quote proves statement; actor not named in the quote (sponsor/applicant inferred).

f.title: Review emerging safety data by qualified experts and adjust ongoing and future studies to protect participants
f.statement: Emerging non-clinical, clinical and pharmaceutical quality data should be reviewed and evaluated, as they become available, by qualified experts to assess the potential implications for the safety of study participants. Ongoing and future studies should be appropriately adjusted as needed to take new knowledge into consideration and to protect study participants.

f.title: Make participant protection the first priority when designing early clinical studies
f.statement: The protection of study participants should always be the first priority when designing early clinical studies, especially for the initial administration of an investigational product to humans (usually referred to as phase 1).
f.applicability: Early clinical studies, especially first administration to humans

rows.quote: The protection of study participants should always be the first priority when designing early clinical studies, especially for the initial administration of an investigational product to humans (usually referred to as phase 1).

f.title: Conduct extended-exposure studies when the drug is intended for long-term administration
f.statement: If the intent is to administer a drug for a long period of time, studies involving extended exposure to the drug should be conducted (ICH E1). Irrespective of the intended duration of administration, the duration of effect of the drug will also inform the duration of follow-up.
f.clause: 4.3.2 Exploratory and Confirmatory Safety and Efficacy Studies
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Epidemiology / safety studies

f.title: Follow up and report the outcome of pregnancies occurring in clinical studies
f.statement: Where pregnant women volunteer to be enrolled in a clinical study, or a participant becomes pregnant while participating in a clinical study, follow-up evaluation of the pregnancy and its outcome and the reporting of outcomes are necessary.
f.applicability: Pregnant women enrolled in, or participants becoming pregnant during, a clinical study
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Where pregnant women volunteer to be enrolled in a clinical study, or a participant becomes pregnant while participating in a clinical study, follow-up evaluation of the pregnancy and its outcome and the reporting of outcomes are necessary.
rows.review_note: Review: level changed Recommended -> Mandatory; the quote itself states follow-up of the pregnancy and outcome and reporting of outcomes 'are necessary'. Double-check: 74 because level changed Mandatory -> Recommended: 'are necessary' in a non-binding ICH guideline is a strong expectation, not shall/must or a legal duty; level remains a judgement call; actor not named in the quote (sponsor/applicant inferred).

f.title: Examine excretion of the drug into human milk where applicable and feasible
f.statement: Excretion of the drug or its metabolites into human milk should be examined where applicable and feasible. When nursing mothers are enrolled in clinical studies, their babies are usually also monitored for the effects of the drug.
f.applicability: Drugs that may be used by lactating women; studies enrolling nursing mothers

f.title: The extent of safety data collection may be tailored where the safety profile is well characterised
f.statement: Where the safety profile of the drug is well characterised, the extent of safety data collection may be tailored to the objectives of the study.
f.applicability: Studies of drugs with a well-characterised safety profile
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety intake & collection

f.title: Ensure study data contain the information needed to monitor participant safety
f.statement: The study data should contain the necessary information to conduct the statistical analysis specified in the protocol and statistical analysis plan, as well as to monitor for participant safety, protocol adherence and data integrity.

rows.quote: The study data should contain the necessary information to conduct the statistical analysis specified in the protocol and statistical analysis plan, as well as to monitor for participant safety, protocol adherence, and data integrity.

f.title: Ensure study data quality is sufficient to monitor participant safety in interventional studies
f.statement: Study data should be of sufficient quality to address the objectives of the study and, in interventional studies, to monitor participant safety.

f.title: Specify procedures and systems for identifying, monitoring and reporting safety concerns during the study
f.statement: Procedures and systems for the identification, monitoring and reporting of safety concerns during the study should be clearly specified, serving the goals of safety monitoring: to protect study participants and to characterise the safety profile of the drug.

f.title: Define clear criteria for stopping treatment or study procedures for a participant
f.statement: Clear criteria for stopping treatment or study procedures for a study participant while remaining in the study are necessary to ensure the protection of participants, but should also minimise loss of critical data.

rows.quote: Clear criteria for stopping treatment or study procedures for a study participant while remaining in the study are necessary to ensure the protection of the participants but should also minimise loss of critical data.

Double-check: 72 because level changed Mandatory -> Recommended: 'are necessary ... but should also' in a non-binding guideline is not shall/must; level remains a judgement call; actor not named in the quote (sponsor/applicant inferred).

f.title: Assess the need for an independent DMC across the programme and establish its procedures before study start
f.statement: During programme planning, the need for an independent data monitoring committee to monitor safety data across studies in a development programme should be assessed. If a data monitoring committee is needed for an individual study or across the programme, procedures governing its operation, in particular the review of unblinded data in an interventional trial while preserving study integrity, should be established prior to study start.

rows.deadline: Procedures established prior to study start
rows.quote: During programme planning, the need for an independent data monitoring committee to monitor safety data across studies in a development programme should also be assessed. If a data monitoring committee is needed for either an individual study or across the development programme, procedures governing its operation and, in particular the review of unblinded data in an interventional trial, while preserving study integrity (ICH E9) should be established prior to study start.
